facts.raw_span: abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus 2 days earlier and migrated to the right lower quadrant
no prior abdominal surgeries or systemic disease
denied anorexia, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, weight loss, night sweats, diarrhea, or constipation
afebrile
heart rate was 86 bpm
blood pressure was 130/95 mm Hg
voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant
minimal tenderness elsewhere
white-cell count of 15,600/mL
hemoglobin of 14.2 g/dL
plain abdominal X-rays demonstrated several air–fluid levels without free air under the diaphragm
ultrasound assessment was interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis

concepts.why: The patient presented with abdominal pain that migrated to the right lower quadrant, which is a classic symptom of appendicitis, and the ultrasound assessment was compatible with plastron appendicitis.
The patient had abdominal pain, voluntary guarding, and minimal tenderness elsewhere, which could indicate a perforated appendix.
The patient presented with abdominal pain and inflammation, which could be indicative of inflammatory bowel disease.
The patient had abdominal pain and tenderness, which could indicate diverticulitis.
The patient presented with abdominal pain and air-fluid levels on X-ray, which could indicate an intestinal obstruction.
The patient had abdominal pain and inflammation, which could be indicative of mesenteric lymphadenitis.
The patient presented with abdominal pain and denied anorexia, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, which could indicate gastroenteritis.
The patient had abdominal pain and air-fluid levels on X-ray, which could indicate intussusception.

rationales.F01: The patient's abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant is a classic symptom of appendicitis.
rationales.F07: Voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant is a sign of peritoneal irritation, which is consistent with appendicitis.
rationales.F09: The elevated white-cell count indicates an inflammatory response, which is consistent with appendicitis.
rationales.F11: The presence of air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays is consistent with an intestinal obstruction, which can be caused by appendicitis.
rationales.F12: The ultrasound assessment compatible with plastron appendicitis provides strong evidence for appendicitis.
